text: <p>Future Legal Regulation of AI Agent Applications in Financial Markets</p> presents the following source proposition: Second, existing legal frameworks—such as data protection and securities regulations—are inherently static and anthropocentric, rendering them ill-equipped to address the adaptive and evolving behavior of AI systems, thereby weakening both disclosure obligations and privacy safeguards. This proposition is pertinent to Kaal's source-bound claim that The EU's Market Abuse, Transparency, Markets in Financial Instruments and Prospectus Directives improved European securities regulation but still do not mandate coherent and comprehensive disclosure, leaving issuers free to disclose in disparate ways.
